rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a 2BA blastocyst and appropriately notes loose ICM and fair TE, but it speculates about collapse/degeneration and calls the embryo lower quality than the provided Gardner score alone supports.
Integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, endometrium, semen parameters, and first-cycle status well, though some interactions are discussed somewhat generically.

Overall logical, but there are internal inconsistencies: it first drifts toward 15–30%, then 25–35%, and ultimately 20–30%, and it somewhat over-penalizes a 2BA embryo while still calling prognosis favorable.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based: SET at age 34, caution about hydrosalpinx, avoid routine add-ons, selective rather than routine PGT-A. Minor issue is somewhat pessimistic interpretation of 2BA morphology.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, cavity/tubal review, and when to escalate evaluation; useful though not highly tailored beyond standard IVF management.
